summary: A pull request covered by our hosts' notes skips CI entirely: sampling is off for every check (sample_one_in 1), a host note is held to the lane as the signed tree defines it (by_level lane "tree"), so a change that edits its own lane is covered by a note made with that edited definition (evidence-wrap now records that digest instead of refusing such a tree), and a change to the files that decide skipping (gate, verifier, policy, keys, lanes, rust-test inputs) is covered on a pull_request run by a host note. The gate and verifier that judge it are still the base's; the merge queue still runs every check in full, and push to main is unchanged.

replay.detail: No record or signature format changes; a note made on a lane-edit tree records the digest of that tree's lane definition in the existing lane_definition_sha256 input.

schema.detail: The skip policy's by_level lane accepts "tree" besides true and false; nothing stored changes.

rules.detail: On pull_request runs: no sampling; host notes may cover lane edits (with the edited definition's digest) and protected-file changes. merge_group runs and every other signer level keep the earlier rules.

compatibility.detail: The gate and verifier are read from the base, so the new rules apply to pull requests opened or re-run after this merges.

recovery.detail: Revert this change: sample_one_in 5, host lane true and the protected fallback come back with the base.
